# Combat content provenance

New work in this change consists of original Youth Fighter JavaScript rules, numeric balance proposals, mentor challenge text, documentation, tests, HUD controls and procedural Canvas anticipation geometry. Names and mechanics in the combat brief are treated as original working proposals requiring further balance/provenance review. No new raster, model, music or recorded audio asset was imported or generated.

The existing hero, movement, map and residential assets under public/assets are reused in place. The previous project documents describe their prior art pipeline; this change does not independently establish their licensing or legal clearance. Fist and Spear use explicit existing pose-column adapters. Hidden/ultimate/defense poses and synthesized hit tones are placeholders, not newly authored martial animation or sound recordings. The initial two-path combat added no new weapon assets. The five-school follow-up adds original procedural Staff, Blade and concealed Dart overlays in hero-render.js and its fallback; it imports no weapon artwork. These are explicit visual placeholders, not authored martial animation sets.

The reference client was inspected read-only for top-level metadata and selected PE headers. No updater or executable was launched, configured service contacted, archive unpacked, code decompiled, or proprietary asset imported. Its names, package categories and version fields are not evidence for Youth Fighter's new combat mechanics. Design differences alone are not a legal-clearance claim.
